findings.title: Unguarded `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` access raises KeyError
findings.body: The sender check does `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` with no guard. `sender` is only stored when the installation webhook (or `build_integration`) supplied it. Integrations created earlier, or created without a sender, will have no `sender` key. In that case the installation view raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the friendly error page. If a missing sender is meant to fail closed, it should be handled explicitly with `.get()` and rendered through `error()`.

findings.title: GitHub user validation is skipped when the Integration row does not exist yet
findings.body: If `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises DoesNotExist, the view calls `pipeline.next_step()` immediately. The `github_authenticated_user` comparison only runs when the Integration row already exists, i.e. after the installation webhook has been processed. If the user returns to Sentry before the webhook arrives, or the webhook is delayed or lost, the check is bypassed. The OAuth step is then pointless, because the authenticated user is never compared with the installer. That fail-open path undermines the security fix.

findings.title: Network and HTTP errors in the OAuth exchange are not handled
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(...)` is called outside the try/except. A connection error, timeout or blocked host will propagate as a 500. `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is also unguarded. It performs a GitHub API call that can raise on HTTP errors (rate limit, 5xx, revoked token), and it can return a body that is not a dict. The PR description says the pipeline should fail with the standard error page, but these paths produce unhandled exceptions.

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL is built without URL-encoding
findings.body: The `state` and `redirect_uri` values are interpolated directly into the query string with an f-string. They should be encoded with `urlencode`. The redirect URI contains `://` and `/`, and the test even asserts the unencoded form. This works only because the current values happen to be safe. It is fragile if the signature format or host ever contains reserved characters.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the installation-not-found path
findings.body: The test now sends a hard-coded `state` of `ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which differs from the pipeline signature. The failure therefore comes from the state-mismatch check in `OAuthLoginView`, and the flow never reaches `build_integration`. The assertion changed from 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' to the generic 'Invalid installation request.', so the 404 handling for a missing installation is no longer covered. There is also no dedicated test for state mismatch, a failed token exchange, or missing `login` in the user info response.

findings.title: Brittle assertion on the index of the recorded HTTP call
findings.body: `responses.calls[2]` assumes the exact number and order of outbound calls made by the OAuth step (token exchange, `/user`, then the JWT call). Any change to that sequence silently breaks the test or checks the wrong request. Filtering the calls by URL would be more robust.
